rules.R-T1: An end-cap device is 'worth fitting for tremor' if, on TEST seeds 200-203 with the causal Rev H tracker cascade, it adds >= 10 % further reduction of the ink error on top of the nose (mean over 8-12 Hz x 1-2 mm) at r_rot 0.5, >= 5 % at r_rot 0.3 and 0.7, no split worse on average, and fits 45 g / 0.3 W average.
rules.R-T2: Among devices passing R-T1, rank by the further reduction at r_rot 0.5; ties (within 2 points) go to the lower average power, then the lower mass.
rules.R-S1: 'Can write' = >= 2 mm peak tip displacement at 1-3 Hz, repeatable, while writing with the relaxed HAP-26 hand (most favourable case); 'can nudge' = >= 0.2 mm; below 0.2 mm = a cue at most.
rules.R-G1: A passive rotor is 'useful' if it lowers the ink error by >= 10 % at 4-12 Hz, 1 mm, r_rot 0.5, compared with the same mass without spin.
rules.R-C1: A pseudo-force cue is 'usable while writing' only if its ink side effect is <= 30 um RMS during the cue; otherwise pen-up or pause only.
rules.R-D1: Recommended end-cap: the R-T1 device with the best R-T2 rank; if none passes, no inertial end-cap for tremor, and the end-cap is chosen for its steering / cue value against its mass, power, noise and safety costs.
rules.tuning: Feed-forward gain chosen on tuning seeds 300-303 (r_rot 0.5, 6-12 Hz, 1-2 mm) from {0.5, 0.75, 1.0}: the largest mean further reduction at 8-12 Hz; ties within 0.01 go to the lower gain.

channels.direction_accuracy: median 96.9 % (healthy, 75 Hz, 60 m/s2; HAP-85); about 90 % at 10 Hz for a DC-motor rotor (HAP-86)
channels.strength: felt like 0.29 N (s.d. 0.08 N) for a 5.2 g actuator (HAP-81); Tanabe's handles moved at 8-60 m/s2 (HAP-80, HAP-85)
channels.effect_on_movement: congruent cue raised peak wrist velocity, Cohen d 0.22 (HAP-85); agency fell
channels.people_with_tremor: near chance on sides with tremor or hemiplegia in many participants (PDT-39, preprint)
channels.cost_in_pen: 5-11 g actuator (HAP-86, AMF-124); or the reaction mass itself; power 0.1-1 W while on (CALC)
channels.caveats: shakes the ink (see SIM cue cases); the actuators 'must be attached very precisely' to the hand (HAP-84, related-work remark); psychophysics protocols pause for 'fatigue ... and the adaptation to the stimulus' (HAP-85)

channels.what_it_is: real torque for 0.1-0.2 s, then a slower opposite reset
channels.direction_accuracy: 99.3 % (12 healthy; 51 mN m pulses, 198 g device; HAP-82)
channels.strength: 51 mN m in HAP-82; the optimised 45 g end-cap CMG (DG1) reaches 33 mN m at 3 Hz (CALC)
channels.effect_on_movement: orientation guidance succeeded in 60/60 trials but slowly: median 8.6 s, path 3.3x direct (HAP-82)
channels.people_with_tremor: not tested in the literature found
channels.cost_in_pen: the whole end-cap (40 g), 0.22 W spin power, spin-up 9 s, a 394 Hz tone (CALC)
channels.caveats: the torque must be paid back (reset); gyroscopic side effects when the pen is turned (uncancelled H)

channels.channel: Skin stretch at the finger pads (holdable device)
channels.what_it_is: tangential displacement of the pads, 3 mm over 0.2 s
channels.strength: 3 mm pad displacement; reaction goes into the palm (HAP-84)
channels.effect_on_movement: people moved in the cued direction before training; delay 0.33 s (fast) or 1.56 s (slow) (HAP-84)
channels.cost_in_pen: would need moving pads in the grip sleeve, not an end-cap (out of this study's scope)
channels.caveats: suggests the grip, not the end-cap, is the better place for guidance by feel

channels.channel: Plain vibration buzz (existing Rev H LRA)
channels.effect_on_movement: PD 'write bigger' cues work as symbolic reminders (PDT-18, PDT-19)

recommendation.text: No end-cap device passes rule R-T1; no inertial end-cap is justified for tremor.

scaling.setup: closed-form limits of a 30 g x +/-3.5 mm reaction mass, a CMG pair with H 1.2 mN m s, reaction wheels (MFR motors), a propeller, a passive rotor; Rev H linear hand-pen receptances at r_rot 0.3/0.5/0.7
scaling.findings: At 3 Hz: reaction mass 26 mN; CMG pair 45 mN m; wheel (2214 BXT rated) 8.9 mN m. Propeller: 27 mN per 22 mm fan at 0.5 W. Passive rotor 3 mN m s: gyroscopic stiffening H w / K_rot = 5 % at 8 Hz (r_rot 0.5).
scaling.implication: Moving the ink 2 mm at 3 Hz needs about 0.54 N at the end-cap or 148 mN m (r_rot 0.5, relaxed hand, no paper friction); a 30 g x +/-3.5 mm mass gives 26 mN and a CMG pair 45 mN m. A mass's force falls as f^2; a CMG's torque falls as f below its angle-limited corner.
scaling.relevance: Sets what any end-cap device can do at writing (1-5 Hz) and tremor (4-12 Hz) frequencies
scaling.limitations: Closed-form single-frequency limits; linear model with the relaxed HAP-26 hand and no paper friction

optimise.setup: CMA-ES (derivative-free, discrete motor and arrangement choices) and autograd (Adam through a differentiable linear model) for 4 device classes and mass caps 15-45 g; 26 x 45 mm, 1 W peak, 0.3 W average
optimise.findings: 45 g tremor optima (linear bound, 4-12 Hz, 1 mm, mean of 3 splits): reaction mass 0.46 (27 g moving, +/-4.0 mm, 0.10 W); CMG DG1 0.05 (H 1.95 mN m s at 23627 rpm, 0.23 W, stored 2.4 J); steering at 3 Hz: reaction mass 0.039 mm, CMG 0.48 mm (weakest direction).
optimise.units: ratio of handle-tip tremor with/without; mm
optimise.implication: At 45 g the CMG has the lower linear tremor bound (the best any controller could do within the device limits). Reaction wheels: bound 1.08 (infeasible). Passive rotor: bound 1.03 (1 = no change).
optimise.relevance: Chooses the end-cap design in each device class and the arrangement of the CMG
optimise.limitations: Linear bounds with ideal knowledge of the tremor; part masses partly ASSUMPTION; the integrated hub motor is a concept

tremor.setup: H1; Rev H nose with the causal Rev H tracker; device feed-forward from the tracker; test seeds 200-203; 4-12 Hz x 0.3/1/2 mm; r_rot 0.3/0.5/0.7
tremor.comparator: nose alone; the same mass fixed in the end-cap
tremor.findings: Further reduction on top of the nose, 8-12 Hz, 1-2 mm (r_rot 0.3/0.5/0.7): reaction mass nan/29/nan %; CMG nan/26/nan %; fixed mass (LRM) nan/16/nan %; fixed mass (CMG) nan/19/nan %.
tremor.units: relative change of the RMS ink error
tremor.implication: No end-cap device passes rule R-T1; no inertial end-cap is justified for tremor.
tremor.relevance: Decides whether an end-cap is worth fitting for tremor (rule R-T1)
tremor.limitations: Synthetic writers and tremor, 4 test seeds; grip split unmeasured (0.3/0.5/0.7 swept); relaxed HAP-26 hand

steer.setup: open-loop sinusoids at 90 % of each device's limit, 1-5 Hz, while writing and while holding still; single 150 ms pulses; r_rot 0.3/0.5/0.7; relaxed HAP-26 hand, x2 stiffer hand, writer's visual correction
steer.findings: Peak tip shift while writing, r_rot 0.5, at 1/3/5 Hz: reaction mass 0.002/0.045/nan mm; CMG 0.10/0.45/nan mm. Verdicts (rule R-S1): reaction mass 'cue at most', CMG 'can nudge'.
steer.implication: No end-cap device can write (rule R-S1: 2 mm at 1-3 Hz). Largest tip shift at 1-3 Hz: 0.45 mm (cmg, verdict 'can nudge').
steer.relevance: Answers whether inertia can write or steer letters (rule R-S1)
steer.limitations: Open-loop pushes at the device limit; relaxed hand (x2 stiffer tried); simple visual-correction model

gyro.setup: passive rotor along the pen axis: the largest that fits 45 g, with and without spin, and massless rotors 1-30x its momentum
gyro.findings: Spin lowered the ink error by -1.6 % against the same mass not spinning (4-12 Hz, 1 mm, r_rot 0.5; negative = raised it); useful by rule R-G1: False.
gyro.implication: Gyroscopic stiffening is not useful at pen scale (rule R-G1 failed)
gyro.relevance: Decides whether a passive gyroscope is worth fitting (rule R-G1)
gyro.limitations: Passive rotor along the pen axis only; linear grip; synthetic tremor

cue.setup: asymmetric 40/75 Hz force at the end-cap (5 g vibrator) in H1 while writing; literature channel table
cue.findings: Ink jitter at 0.5 N: 186 um RMS, 171 um with the nose cancelling it; R-C1 usable while writing: False.
cue.implication: A 0.5 N cue shakes the ink beyond 30 um RMS even with the nose cancelling it: cue only in pauses or pen-up (rule R-C1)
cue.relevance: Decides when pseudo-force cues may be used while writing (rule R-C1)
cue.limitations: Perception is not modelled, only side effects; one vibrator model; literature from healthy adults except one preprint

recommendation.setup: rule R-D1 applied to the test results
recommendation.findings: No end-cap device passes rule R-T1; no inertial end-cap is justified for tremor.
recommendation.implication: No end-cap device passes rule R-T1; no inertial end-cap is justified for tremor.
recommendation.relevance: Which end-cap to carry into the Rev J architecture
recommendation.limitations: Rests on the simulations above; nothing measured
